title: Finite free cancellation of a split top differential
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n\in\mathbf Z$. Let $P^\bullet$ be a cochain complex of $R$-modules, that is modules $P^i$ and maps $d^i:P^i\to P^{i+1}$ with $d^{i+1}d^i=0$. Suppose $P^i=0$ for $i>n$ and every $P^i$ is finite free (isomorphic to $R^{r_i}$ for some finite $r_i$). Given an $R$-linear section $s:P^n\to P^{n-1}$ satisfying $d^{n-1}s=1_{P^n}$, there exist a cochain complex $L^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules, with $L^i=0$ for $i>n-1$, and a chain map $\pi:L^\bullet\to P^\bullet$ inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology modules $H^i=\ker d^i/\operatorname{im}d^{i-1}$. No lower bound is assumed.

source.place: Tag 064U, Lemma 15.66.5, finite-free replacement by identity complexes; split-top cancellation in step 3 of lem-pc-pseudo-coherent-bounded-finite-free-model. Source read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064U.

proof.text: Put m=n-1 and T=P^n. The cycles of P at m are the kernel of d:P^m → T. The given section s splits the short exact kernel sequence, giving the explicit isomorphism cycles(P,m) ⊕ T ≅ P^m. This uses ShortComplex.Splitting.ofExactOfSection and cyclesIsKernel.

Construct K=truncLE(m)P and A=mappingCone(id(single(m,T))); define L=K ⊕ A. The cone A is the identity two-term complex in degrees m-1,m and hence is contractible. Both K and A vanish above m. Below m, terms of K are isomorphic to the original finite free terms of P; terms of A are biproducts of zero or T and are finite free. At m, K^m=cycles(P,m) and A^m≅T, so the splitting in step 1 identifies L^m with the original finite free P^m. Above m the terms are zero, also finite free. Thus L is supported at most m and all its terms are finite free.

Prove P is cohomologically supported at most m. At n=m+1, the section makes d:P^m → P^n epic and the outgoing differential is zero, hence the short complex is exact. All higher terms of P are zero and hence exact. The canonical inclusion K → P is therefore a quasi-isomorphism by CochainComplex.quasiIso_ιTruncLE_iff.

The identity of A is homotopic to zero by mappingCone.homotopyToZeroOfId, so its map on every homology object is both the identity and zero. Therefore H^i(A) is a zero object. Under the additive homology functor, the two biproduct identities show that the map induced by L → K has inverse the map induced by K → L: the contribution through H^i(A) vanishes. Hence L → K is a quasi-isomorphism. Its composite with K → P is the required π. All constructions use the supplied section and Mathlib truncations and cones, with no witness selected from an unproved existence theorem.

mathlib_searches.query: A split top differential of a bounded above finite free cochain complex can be cancelled by a quasi-isomorphic finite free complex with upper bound lowered by one
A bounded above finite free cochain complex with a split top differential is quasi-isomorphic to a finite free complex whose upper bound is one smaller

lean.statement:
theorem exists_finiteFree_cancel_split_top
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (n : ℤ)
    (hbound : P.IsStrictlyLE n)
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (P.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (P.X i))
    (s : P.X n ⟶ P.X (n - 1)) (hs : s ≫ P.d (n - 1) n = 𝟙 (P.X n)) :
    ∃ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{v} R) ℤ) (π : L ⟶ P),
      L.IsStrictlyLE (n - 1) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Free R (L.X i) ∧ Module.Finite R (L.X i)) ∧
      QuasiIso π
